extracted.intended_audience: students, writers, critics, and general readers studying or working in magical realism across literature, visual art, film, and games
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and distinguishing characteristics for creating or identifying magical realism across media (literature, visual art, film, games), including narrative stance, thematic registers, and formal techniques that separate it from realism, surrealism, fantasy, and fabulism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantastic elements embedded in everyday reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Fantastic (magical) elements appear as part of everyday reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magical occurrences are presented as ordinary, integrated aspects of the real world rather than as disruptions. They should function within the texture of quotidian life, not as spectacles separate from it. Example use: ghosts, miracles or impossible events narrated as normal facts of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective narration aligned with traditional realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective narration characteristic of traditional, 19th-century realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narration often uses a dispassionate, matter-of-fact voice (rather than overtly lyrical or psychologizing modes) to report magical events, which increases the effect of the marvelous by treating it as unremarkable. This objective stance helps sustain reader acceptance of the extraordinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic/tonal registers of magic realism (myth, defamiliarization, mysticism, meta-narration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magic realism encompasses terms such as 'myth/legend', 'fantastic/supplementation', 'defamiliarization', 'mysticism/magic', 'meta-narration', 'open-ended/expansive romanticism', and 'imagination/negative capability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these registers to orient tone and meaning: mythic references, deliberate estrangement of the familiar, mystical or supra-rational elements, narrative self-reflection, and openness rather than reductive closure. These contrast with realism's emphasis on empiricism, cause-and-effect, and closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary not presented as dream/psychological experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical realism rarely presents the extraordinary in the form of a dream or a psychological experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid framing magic as solely interior (subconscious or dream states). Instead, present marvels as tangible events in shared material reality. This differentiates magical realism from surrealism, which foregrounds the inner life, unconscious, or dream imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabulism vs magical realism: myth-specific borrowing and allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabulism incorporates fantasy elements into reality using myths and fables—often borrowing specific myths, fairy tales, and folktales to critique the exterior world and offer allegorical interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing/evaluating fabulist works expect direct borrowings from known stories and an allegorical/moralizing bent. By contrast, magical realism more often uses generalized magic embedded in social/political reality and (traditionally) may be tied to particular cultural/political contexts (e.g., Latin America).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chanady's three dimensions distinguishing fantasy and magic realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences across three dimensions: the use of antinomy (simultaneous presence of two conflicting codes), inclusion of events that cannot be integrated into a logical framework, and the use of authorial reticence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these axes when classifying a text: fantasy tends to treat the supernatural as a separate problematic code and emphasize hesitation/strangeness, while magic realism presents conflicting codes side-by-side as equally valid and often uses authorial restraint to normalize the marvelous rather than explain or integrate it fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supernatural perceived as problematic (fantasy) vs accepted (magical realism)
rubrics_metrics.description: In fantasy, the presence of the supernatural code is perceived as problematic and draws special attention; in magical realism, the presence of the supernatural is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate narrator/characterial reaction: if the narrative highlights puzzlement, disbelief, or attempts to rationalize the supernatural it leans toward fantasy/fantastic literature; if the narrative treats it as ordinary and unquestioned, it aligns with magical realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hesitation (the fantastic) versus seamless blending
rubrics_metrics.description: Fantastic literature creates a hesitation between attributing events to natural or supernatural causes; magical realism blends the supernatural with the natural so that readers accept the marvelous as normal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key diagnostic is whether protagonist/reader experience unsettled faltering between belief and non-belief (fantastic) versus a stable acceptance where both codes coexist as 'twofold' reality (magical realism). Examples: Kafka's The Metamorphosis (hesitation) vs García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude (acceptance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Twofold world (blend of supernatural and natural)
rubrics_metrics.description: In magical realism, the supernatural realm blends with the natural, familiar world — a 'twofold' world — as opposed to the single-world structure of fairy-tale and fantasy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worldbuilding should allow coexisting explanatory codes without hierarchizing them; supernatural events occur within recognizable settings and are narrated as part of that reality. Example: ghosts presented as ordinary occurrences in One Hundred Years of Solitude and Beloved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roh's visual-art definition: intense realism that reveals interior mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Roh applied 'magic realism' to visual art as a style that brings extreme realism to mundane subject matter, revealing an 'interior' mystery rather than imposing overt magical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In visual media aim for faithful, detailed depiction of ordinary objects/scenes such that their representation evokes an implicit mystery or magic. The effect is produced by realism's intensity rather than by added fantastical props.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roh's pictorial features: ordinary subjects, forward movement vs distance, miniature detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Other important aspects of magical realist painting (according to Roh) include: a return to ordinary subjects; a juxtaposition of forward movement with a sense of distance; and the use of miniature details even in expansive paintings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mundane subject matter, compositional tension between near and far, and concentrated fine detail within broader canvases to create estrangement and a sense of hidden depth. These techniques produce a 'magic' in the viewer's interpretation rather than adding explicit fantasy elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magic via faithful rendering, not arbitrary alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: The magic effect often arises from the intensity of faithful rendering of reality rather than from arbitrary changes to what is seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inventing gratuitous supernatural gimmicks; instead, deepen observation and precise depiction so that the ordinary yields uncanny meanings. Quote example: John Stuart Ingle aims to 'paint what is given' and explore that reality intensely to evoke the magic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mid-20th-century visual trend: overt fantastical elements anchored in everyday reality
rubrics_metrics.description: By mid-20th century 'magic realism' in visual art came to refer to work that incorporates overtly fantastic elements while remaining anchored in everyday reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contemporary practitioners may include explicit surreal or magical motifs but keep them embedded in recognizably real settings; look for stylized distortions or exaggerations that create a surreal atmosphere without constructing wholly separate fantasy worlds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film/TV presentation: matter-of-fact magical events and cinematic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: In film and television, magical realist characteristics are often presented matter-of-factly and occur without explanation; cinematic tools (e.g., first-person framing, child's POV, color heightening) can establish the magical-realist storytelling frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting or evaluating screen narratives, expect the marvelous to be integrated into the diegesis and supported by formal choices that normalize or heighten its presence (voice-over framing, perspective choice, stylized color palettes), rather than by explicit exposition of supernatural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive/new-media manifestations (video games, electronic literature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Video games and electronic literature can display magic-realist qualities by combining realistic settings and technologies with ambiguous or supernatural elements; some scholars argue games' intrinsic structure supports magic realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for interactive works that place fantastical events into otherwise plausible systems (e.g., military realism plus supernatural elements in Metal Gear, point-and-click adventures like Kentucky Route Zero). Ambiguity, branching lexias, and player-guided perspective can reinforce the genre's twofold reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial aim: blur boundary between real and fantastic
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorial aim of magical realism is 'destroying the line of demarcation that separates what seems real from what seems fantastic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In both creation and critique, assess how the text intentionally undermines the reader's neat separation of realism and the marvelous—through narrative stance, cultural/mythic layering, and formal technique—so that the extraordinary reads as part of the world rather than as a separate invention.
